paragraphs: The anti-GoodRx. GoodRx and OptimizeRx get paid by PBMs and pharma, so they're structurally incentivized to steer patients toward whoever pays them. This has one job: find every legal way a specific patient pays less, even when it costs the drug company or the PBM money. No PBM fee revenue, no pharma placement revenue, ever. That's the entire moat.
Not a treatment tool. Doesn't touch diagnosis, doesn't touch clinical decisions. It only touches money: prices, program terms, accumulator policy, formulary tiers.
The database of exploits is the actual asset. The frontend is disposable. Structure:
features: Brain (Supabase project): drugs, pricepoints, exploits, accumulatorpolicies,
Frontend (Next.js, Vercel): thin. Takes patient inputs (drug, dose, state,
Monitor (scheduled job): the "trained AI" part. Watches for formulary
